notes:
Klipr 2.14 — Streamers, AI Review and Settings redesigned

**Streamers**
- Every streamer now has its own ACTIVE switch. On means Klipr watches that
  channel, off pauses just that one without removing it or losing its custom
  threshold. The old Pause/Resume button at the bottom is gone.
- Rebuilt as a proper table: live indicator, platform and status badges,
  threshold and URL. Double-click a row to edit its threshold, as before.
- Your selection now survives the two-minute live-status refresh instead of
  clearing itself mid-click.

**AI Review**
- The selected clip panel is permanent. It used to appear only after you
  clicked a row, so the page jumped every time the selection changed.
- Upload Schedule is now a single card: enable switch, posting window, and
  the daily cap.
- Queue rows show the headline first, with streamer, chat score, AI score and
  the scheduled time underneath. Statuses are spelled out rather than cut off
  mid-word.
- Fixed: editing a headline on a clip that had no upload time yet crashed the
  page loader and blanked the entire queue. The clip was fine; the list just
  stopped drawing.

**Settings**
- Reorganised into numbered cards across two columns, with each control
  labelled above rather than squeezed beside a long name.
- Save Changes is now pinned to the bottom of the page instead of sitting at
  the end of a long scroll.
- New: Reset Defaults. It loads Klipr's shipped defaults into the form and
  saves nothing until you press Save Changes, so a misclick costs a page
  refresh rather than your configuration. It leaves your Groq key alone.
- The session-recording disk note now sits with the session-recording setting
  instead of several sections away.

**Window sizing**
- Klipr now opens at 1280x720 so Settings shows both columns, and will not
  shrink below 1060x700 — under that, some controls had nowhere to render.
